answer: The admission bond is time locked for 16 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are recorded in cipher, expire in wharf, and atlas lists each expiry. An adversary running 167 aliases hence needs 112 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. A farm of 2689 identities would post 2463 proofs and burn roughly 32 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
